# QDA-SQL: Questions Enhanced Dialogue Augmentation for Multi-Turn Text-to-SQL

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#qda-sql)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2406.10593v3) · arXiv:2406.10593v3, 16 July 2026; 10 PDF pages

**Reading coverage:** All substantive text Sections I-VIII, Tables I-VIII and figures. Rendered pages 5, 6, 8, 9 inspected to recover encoded chart labels and compare tables. No appendices.

## Research question

SQL-only dialogue fine-tuning can leave systems unable to clarify ambiguous questions, refuse unsupported requests or handle non-database conversation.

## Method

Combines goal SQL, four thematic relations and four question types to synthesize dialogues; LLM alignment checks, expression refinement and execution checks filter outputs. StateFlow separates intent recognition, SQL generation and execution-error repair.

## Evaluation

Generates 10,874 dialogues/65,393 turns from SParC and CoSQL training data. QLoRA experiments report query/interaction match and classification; AccS combines classification with SQL matching only for answerable turns. Quality evidence includes 50 misclassified samples and GPT-4 pairwise judgments.

## What the results support

Mixed-type training improves intent recognition relative to SQL-only training, while SQL-only augmentation sometimes yields better SQL matching. CoSQL ambiguity and unanswerability F1 remain 20% each for the displayed mixed-type model; verification ablation gains are modest.

## Limits and qualifications

The taxonomy includes absent database values as unanswerable, so labels should not be equated with missing-schema impossibility. Nonanswerable AccS rewards the type label, not response quality. Reported mixed-type CoSQL QM differs between Tables V(50.9) andVI(55.9) without a clear reconciliation.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Useful synthetic training and routing baseline, with limited evidence for reliable clarification or refusal in real conversations.
